evals.prompt: take a screenshot of our dashboard at localhost and tell me if the revenue chart is rendering
evals.expected_output: Avoids the capture flags that produce false negatives, verifies the served app is ours, and interrogates the DOM before reporting a rendering fault.
expectations: The dev server is started on a pinned unusual port with strict port enforcement
The response verifies the served page is the expected application rather than another project on that port
The response polls for readiness rather than sleeping a fixed duration
Virtual time is not used, or the response explains it blanks animated chart content
captureBeyondViewport is avoided in favour of a tall window or a measured clip
The DOM is interrogated before any rendering bug is reported
The response states that it actually looked at the resulting image
Page errors are collected and reported alongside the image

evals.prompt: the chart in this screenshot is empty, looks like our data pipeline is broken. can you confirm?
evals.expected_output: Checks whether the capture is at fault before accepting the conclusion, since an empty-looking chart is the signature of a bad capture.
expectations: The response does not immediately accept that the data pipeline is broken
The response checks the DOM for the presence of chart elements and path data
The response checks whether the capture used virtual time or captureBeyondViewport
The response explains that these capture options produce images that look exactly like missing data
The response distinguishes a healthy DOM with a bad capture from genuinely absent data

evals.prompt: our docs screenshots are from an old version of the UI. regenerate them please. we have a demo mode.
evals.expected_output: Uses demo mode rather than a real account, and pins window size and scale so the images stay comparable.
expectations: Demo or fixture mode is used rather than a real logged-in account
The response explains documentation screenshots are published so must not contain real data
Window size and device scale factor are pinned for consistency between runs
An existing screenshot script is used where one exists so images are captured the same way
The response reads the resulting images rather than assuming they rendered as intended
